title: Paloma Top-Up & Bill Pay Disputes on Delivered Orders
content:
A Paloma Top-Up & Bill Pay customer may dispute an order recorded as delivered when the destination says it was not credited, the amount was wrong, a token does not work, or a bill shows unpaid. The filing period, the decision period, whether the product delivers a token and its token re-send limit are the product's own settings.

## Disputes team rules

- **Filing period.** A dispute can be filed only within the product's dispute period in calendar days after the order was delivered. The window is counted in calendar days from the date part of the delivery moment recorded on the order, and a dispute on the last day is on time.
- **One dispute.** Only one dispute per order. Whether a dispute has already been filed on the order is read from the order's case file.
- **Decision.** Paloma checks with the operator or biller and decides within the product's decision period in calendar days after the dispute. Upheld refunds the order value and the fees; rejected leaves the order delivered.
- **Tokens.** Before a token dispute, the token is re-sent to the customer up to the product's token re-send limit, counted as the re-sends logged on the order over its whole life, when the product delivers a token code.

The delivery moment and the case file are Paloma's records of the order; the customer's own recollection of when the order arrived does not move the start of the window.

## Grounds restated

The rule names four grounds on which a delivered order may be disputed: the destination says the order was not credited; the amount was wrong; a token does not work; a bill shows unpaid. Each concerns an order recorded as delivered.

## Counting the filing window

The last day of the window is the delivery date (the date part of the delivery moment) plus the product's number of calendar days. A dispute filed on any day up to and including that last day is on time; a dispute filed on the following day cannot be filed.

**Boundary cases (hypothetical dates; a 30-day period is assumed for illustration).**

| Delivered | Last day to file | Dispute filed | On time? |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 April at 22:40 | 1 May | 1 May at 16:00 | yes — on the last day |
| 1 April at 22:40 | 1 May | 2 May at 09:00 | no — after the window |

## Points of judgement (hypothetical orders)

- An order whose status is failed is not recorded as delivered, so it is not open to a dispute under this rule.
- An order that already has a dispute in its case file, upheld or rejected, cannot be disputed a second time.
- A dispute that Paloma rejects leaves the order delivered; a dispute that Paloma upholds refunds the order value and the fees.
